title: Integrator callback registry
preamble:
# Integrator callback registry

The complete inventory of callbacks an integrator registers with libds. For
each: shape, when it fires, the lifetime of the pointers it receives,
return-value semantics, and what happens when it is not registered.

libds's entire surface to anything outside its own process is **typed C
callbacks plus structured event payloads**. If your integration must bridge libds across processes
or machines (cross-tier publish, remote storage, an external debugger), that
protocol is yours to design — libds hands you typed values; you encode them
however your stack likes.

## What this is not

- Not the first-time walk-through — see [NGST].
- Not the lifecycle guide — [NLFC] covers pump and
  threading; this doc assumes it.
- Not the storage / series detail — the samples-plane callbacks are summarised
  here ([NCBK.12]) and specified under NSTG / NSBK.
